statement: An electric company charges a household $C(k)$ dollars for using $k$ kilowatt-hours of electricity in a month, where $$C(k) = \begin{cases} 0.12k & \text{if } 0 \le k \le 500 \\ 60 + 0.18(k - 500) & \text{if } k > 500 \end{cases}$$ What is the charge for a month in which the household uses $740$ kilowatt-hours?

choices.misconception: I found the charge for the hours above $500$, $0.18 \cdot 240 = 43.20$, but I forgot to add the $\$60$ for the first $500$ kilowatt-hours.
I used the first rule, $0.12 \cdot 740$, without checking that $740$ is more than $500$.
I charged $\$0.18$ for all $740$ kilowatt-hours, but only the kilowatt-hours above $500$ cost that higher rate.

hints: Since $740 > 500$, use the second rule. Only the kilowatt-hours above $500$ are charged at $\$0.18$.

solutions.reliable: Because $740 > 500$, the second rule applies: $C(740) = 60 + 0.18(740 - 500) = 60 + 0.18 \cdot 240 = 60 + 43.20 = 103.20$. The charge is $\$103.20$. (The $60$ is the cost of the first $500$ kilowatt-hours at $\$0.12$ each.)
